summary: Describes Unidirectional Lightweight Encapsulation, a way to carry IPv4, IPv6, and other network packets directly over an MPEG-2 Transport Stream. It specifies a base format and an extension format for extra header information. It is on the standards track.

plainLanguage.summary: Internet packets get wrapped in small envelopes designed for television signals so they can travel by satellite or broadcast.

questions: how to send ip over mpeg-2 transport stream
what is the ule end indicator
subtitle: A thin wrapper that lets IPv4 and IPv6 packets ride inside the fixed 188-byte packets of digital TV broadcasts.

tldr.problem: MPEG-2 Transport Streams, built for digital TV, are also used to build IP networks, but the existing way to carry IP over them (MPE) is heavier to parse and process.
tldr.mechanism: ULE wraps each packet in a small SNDU with a 15-bit length, a 16-bit type, an optional 6-byte receiver address and a CRC-32 trailer, then slices it across 188-byte TS Packets that share one PID.
tldr.outcome: IPv4, IPv6 and bridged Ethernet frames can be carried over one-way broadcast links, with extension headers for later features. RFC 7280 updates this document.

today: RFC 4326 is a Proposed Standard published in December 2005 and is updated by RFC 7280. It has not been obsoleted.

sections.title: Why Carry IP in a TV Stream
sections.content:
The MPEG-2 Transport Stream (TS) was built to deliver digital TV, but it is also used as a subnetwork technology for IP networks. Unidirectional Lightweight Encapsulation (ULE) defines how to carry IPv4 and IPv6 datagrams, and other network-layer packets, directly over a TS as private data. The RFC says its header is significantly simpler to parse and process than alternatives such as MPE, which builds on the DSM-CC Table Section syntax.

An Encapsulator takes each Protocol Data Unit (PDU), such as an Ethernet frame or IP datagram, and turns it into a SubNetwork Data Unit (SNDU) by adding a header and an integrity-check trailer. The SNDU is cut into one or more TS Packets sent on a single TS Logical Channel. A Receiver filters on the channel and rebuilds the SNDUs.

The underlying systems, such as DVB and ATSC, are simplex (one-way). Return channels can still be added, for example two-way satellite links or dial-up modem links. ULE streams can be flagged in the Programme Map Table with a descriptor carrying the format_identifier 0x554C4531, or by the stream_type 0x91.
sections.plainLanguage: Television signals travel in lots of identical small boxes. ULE is a way to pack internet mail into those boxes, so the same broadcast that carries TV can carry web traffic too.

sections.title: How an SNDU Rides in TS Packets
sections.content:
An SNDU goes into the payload of a single TS Packet or, if needed, is fragmented over several. When there is room, one TS Packet may hold more than one SNDU, or parts of them. This is called Packing. All TS Packets of an SNDU MUST carry the same PID, so they stay in one logical channel.

ULE uses the TS header's one-bit Payload Unit Start Indicator (PUSI). Value 0 means the packet continues or ends an SNDU. Value 1 means an SNDU starts in this packet, and a one-byte Payload Pointer follows the TS header. Unused space at the end of a payload is filled with 0xFF bytes, called Padding.

ULE does not use Adaptation Field stuffing. Encapsulators MUST send TS Packets with an Adaptation Field Control value of 01, and Receivers MUST discard packets with other values.
sections.plainLanguage: Imagine sending a long letter in many same-sized boxes. The first box says where the letter begins, and any empty space gets stuffed with filler so nobody mistakes it for letter.

sections.title: The SNDU Format
sections.content:
An SNDU is a header, an optional destination address, the PDU and a CRC-32 trailer. The first bit of the 2-byte length word is the D bit (Destination Address Absent). D=0 means a 6-byte destination address follows the Type field. D=1 means it is left out. The remaining 15 bits are the Length, counted in bytes from the byte after the Type field up to and including the CRC. An End Indicator is the value 0xFFFF (all-ones length with D=1), which tells the Receiver there are no more SNDUs in this TS Packet.

The 16-bit Type field is split like Ethernet's. Values below 1536 (0x0600) are ULE Next-Header values, assigned by IANA. Values of 1536 and above are the IANA EtherType values, for example 0x0800 for IPv4 and 0x86DD for IPv6.

The optional destination address is a 6-byte Network Point of Attachment (NPA) that identifies receivers. It MUST be present for IP unicast to routers on shared links. The value 0x00:00:00:00:00:00 MUST NOT be used, and 0xFF:FF:FF:FF:FF:FF is the broadcast address. IP multicast groups are mapped to NPA multicast addresses as Ethernet does.

Every SNDU ends with a 32-bit CRC computed with the CRC-32 generator polynomial 0x104C11DB7, starting from an accumulator of 0xFFFF FFFF. Receivers discard any SNDU with a bad CRC.
sections.plainLanguage: Each packet gets a label with its size, what kind of thing is inside, and optionally who it is for. A check number on the end lets the receiver tell if the packet got scrambled on the way.

sections.title: Extension Headers
sections.content:
A Type value below 1536 signals an Extension Header instead of a payload. The 16-bit Type is laid out as a 5-bit zero prefix, a 3-bit H-LEN and an 8-bit H-Type. H-LEN of 0 means a Mandatory Extension Header, whose length is predefined and which may change how the enclosed PDU is encoded (for example by encryption or compression). H-LEN 1 to 5 means an Optional Extension Header of 2 to 10 bytes in total, which Receivers that do not understand it may ignore. Several headers can be chained, ending with a Type of 1536 or more that names the real payload.

Three extensions are defined. The Test SNDU (Type 0x0000) carries data that a Receiver may log but MUST discard. The Bridged Frame SNDU (Type 0x0001) carries a whole MAC frame with its MAC destination, MAC source and EtherType or LLC length, so ULE can bridge Ethernet. The Extension-Padding option (0x0100) lets a sender insert one to five 16-bit words, of which only the last, the next Type, is meaningful.

For bridged frames the Encapsulator checks the LAN frame check sequence, drops frames with a bad one, and removes it, relying on the ULE CRC-32 instead. The RFC notes this means corruption inside the Encapsulator or Receiver might not be caught by the final recipient.
sections.plainLanguage: The label can say "there is an extra sticker here" before the real contents. Some stickers are required reading, and some you can skip if you do not know what they mean.

sections.title: Encapsulator Rules: Padding and Packing
sections.content:
After a quiet period, the first TS Packet of an SNDU MUST have PUSI=1 and a Payload Pointer of zero. The MPEG-2 Continuity Counter MUST go up by one (modulo 16) for each TS Packet on the channel.

When an SNDU ends, the Encapsulator has five options depending on the space left in the TS Packet:

  • No space left: send the packet and start the next SNDU in a new one.
  • One byte left: fill it with 0xFF and start the next SNDU in a new packet.
  • Exactly two bytes left with PUSI not set: fill with 0xFFFF, an End Indicator, so the Length field is never split over two packets.
  • More than two bytes left: optionally send the packet after filling the rest with 0xFF. This trades efficiency for lower latency.
  • Enough room to continue: pack the next SNDU right after, setting PUSI to 1 and inserting a Payload Pointer if needed.

An Encapsulator may wait for more PDUs to fill a packet, but that wait, the Packing Threshold, MUST be bounded and SHOULD be configurable.
sections.plainLanguage: If a box is nearly full after packing a letter, you can either put the next letter right in, or stuff the leftover space with filler and ship it now. Shipping now is quicker but wastes space.

sections.title: Receiver Processing
sections.content:
A Receiver tunes to a TS Multiplex, filters on one PID, and reassembles SNDUs independently for each TS Logical Channel. It has two states. In the Idle State it discards TS Packets until one has PUSI=1. It then skips as many bytes as the Payload Pointer says and enters the Reassembly State. A Payload Pointer above 181 is illegal and aborts reassembly.

In Reassembly, the Receiver reads the 2-byte Length. A value of 4 or less, or 0xFFFF, sends it back to Idle. Once all bytes arrive it checks the CRC and discards the SNDU if it is wrong. With D=0 it silently drops SNDUs whose address does not match its own NPA, the broadcast address or a wanted multicast address. An unknown Type below 1536 is discarded.

Receivers must also check the Transport Error Indicator, and the Continuity Counter. Repeated counter values mean duplicate TS Packets, which are discarded. A jump in the counter means lost data, so any partial SNDU is dropped and the Receiver returns to Idle.
sections.plainLanguage: The receiver waits for a box marked "a new letter starts here", then collects boxes until it has the whole letter. If a box is missing or damaged, it throws the half-built letter away and waits for a fresh start.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The RFC says ULE's security considerations resemble those of MPE and that it adds no specific new threats to the general Internet. It lists known issues. Uninitialised stuffing bytes are a known security issue, so ULE sets them to 0xFF. Removing the LAN FCS for bridged frames exposes traffic to undetected corruption. A frame carrying two length fields, as with bridged LLC frames, must be checked, and frames with an LLC Length greater than the SNDU payload size MUST be discarded.

The RFC also anticipates a future Mandatory Extension Header for link encryption of the SNDU payload, as an addition to, not a replacement for, security at the IP, transport or application layer. The encryption method and key exchange are left out of scope.
sections.plainLanguage: The main safety rules are to fill empty space with a known filler instead of leftover junk, and to double-check sizes. Real secret-keeping is left for later add-ons.

fields.name: D
fields.desc: Destination Address Absent: 0 means the address is present.

fields.name: Length
fields.desc: Bytes after the Type field up to and including the CRC.

fields.name: Type
fields.desc: Next-Header below 1536, or an EtherType such as 0x0800.

fields.name: Receiver Destination NPA Address
fields.desc: Optional 6-byte address of the receiver or receivers.

fields.name: CRC-32
fields.desc: Trailer covering the SNDU from the header start up to the CRC.

items.label: Test SNDU
items.desc: Mandatory extension; Receivers discard the data.

items.label: Bridged Frame
items.desc: Mandatory extension carrying a bridged MAC frame.

items.label: Extension-Padding
items.desc: Optional extension of one to five 16-bit words.

transitions.label: End Indicator or insufficient unused space
MPEG-2 TS error or SNDU error
